reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Confusing brief (−2) and sustained (−1) eye contact.
name: Richmond Agitation–Sedation Scale
purpose: Standardised description of agitation and sedation depth.

calculatorNotice.title: Compare with the target
calculatorNotice.message: RASS describes arousal. The appropriate level depends on the sedation target set for the patient.

inputDefinitions.label: Observed level

options.label: +4 Combative
options.detail: Overtly combative or violent; immediate danger to staff.

options.label: +3 Very agitated
options.detail: Pulls on or removes tubes or catheters; aggressive.

options.label: +2 Agitated
options.detail: Frequent non-purposeful movement; fights the ventilator.

options.label: +1 Restless
options.detail: Anxious; movements not aggressive or vigorous.

options.label: −1 Drowsy
options.detail: Sustained (>10 s) awakening with eye contact to voice.

options.label: −2 Light sedation
options.detail: Briefly (<10 s) awakens with eye contact to voice.

options.label: −3 Moderate sedation
options.detail: Movement or eye opening to voice, no eye contact.

options.label: −4 Deep sedation
options.detail: No response to voice; movement or eye opening to physical stimulation.

options.label: −5 Unarousable
options.detail: No response to voice or physical stimulation.

inputDefinitions.help: Observe; if not alert, address by name; use physical stimulation only if there is no response to voice.

resultStates.label: Severe agitation
resultStates.summary: Agitation with risk to patient or staff safety.
resultStates.detail: Assess for pain, delirium, hypoxia, withdrawal and other causes according to local protocol.

resultStates.label: Alert and calm
resultStates.summary: Alert and calm at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Delirium can be present in an alert, calm patient; screen separately.

resultStates.label: Deep sedation or unarousable
resultStates.detail: Whether this is appropriate depends on the sedation target. Delirium screening is not possible at this level.

clinicalContext.text: A standard ICU arousal scale and the first step of CAM-ICU delirium screening.

clinicalInsights.text: Delirium screening (e.g. CAM-ICU) is possible at RASS −3 or above.

limitations.text: Depends on response to voice: limited in deafness, language barriers or neurological deficits.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: The cause of agitation or reduced arousal.

guideSections.whenToUse: Sedation titration and arousal assessment in ICU.
guideSections.howToPerform: Observe for 30 s; address by name; then physical stimulation if no response to voice.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Compared with an individualised sedation target.

sources.citation: Sessler CN, Gosnell MS, Grap MJ, et al. The Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale: validity and reliability in adult intensive care unit patients. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2002;166(10):1338-1344.
